summary: At just three square miles, Muscoy is a census-designated place tucked into the unincorporated flatlands north of San Bernardino, sitting on the alluvial plain where the San Bernardino Mountains rise abruptly to the north — meaning residents get dramatic, close-range views of peaks topping 10,000 feet without any foothills to obscure them. That mountain backdrop belies a ground-level reality shaped by the Inland Empire's logistics economy: massive warehouse and distribution corridors along the I-215 and I-15 freeways are the dominant employers within commuting range, and most working residents drive outward to reach them. A median household income of roughly $57,700 against a median home value of $379,200 produces a price-to-income ratio above 6.5, which pushes conventional homeownership out of comfortable reach for a household earning the local median; median rent at $1,766 consumes well over a third of that same gross income. The area lacks a defined commercial core — no walkable downtown strip, no concentration of sit-down restaurants — and the street grid is fragmented by vacant lots and light-industrial parcels rather than connected parks or trail networks. With 9.6 hours of daily sunshine and average highs around 77°F, the climate is classically sun-drenched inland Southern California, hot in summer but mild in winter. Muscoy is essentially a place where proximity to mountain scenery and relatively lower housing costs coexist with limited local amenities and heavy dependence on the regional freeway network for both employment and daily errands.
